describ: Morning commute — the rhythmic clatter of the subway merges with announcements echoing off tiled walls.
title: Morning Commute

describ: Lunch break at the open-air food market: sizzling woks and vendors calling out the day's specials.
title: Food Market at Noon

describ: A park fountain drowns out distant traffic — water and wind in slow rotation.
title: Park Fountain

describ: A street musician near the subway exit plays an erhu. Passersby slow without stopping.
title: Street Musician

describ: Children's voices bounce off courtyard walls — jump rope counts, laughter, one brief dispute.
title: Children in Courtyard

describ: The temple bell rings at sunset. Three slow strikes that make the whole block pause.
title: Temple Bell at Dusk

describ: Rain drumming on a bus shelter roof — irregular, then steady, then irregular again.
title: Rain on Bus Shelter

describ: A construction site heard from two blocks away: the low thud of pile driving on a schedule.
title: Distant Construction

describ: Coffee shop ambient layer: milk frother, quiet jazz, overlapping conversations just below comprehension.
title: Coffee Shop Hum

describ: Night market coming alive — smoke from grills, plastic stools scraping pavement, someone haggling loudly.
title: Night Market

describ: Rush-hour intersection: mopeds accelerate in gaps between lights, horns used as punctuation.
title: Moped Intersection

describ: Pre-dawn park — only birds and a distant sweeper. The city hasn't started yet.
title: Birds at Dawn

describ: Factory whistle marks shift change. Workers stream through a gate while a new crowd lines up.
title: Factory Whistle

describ: A river boat horn — two blasts, low and long — rolls across the water and fades into the embankment.
title: River Boat Horn

describ: School bell triggers a wave of sound: chairs, voices, feet on linoleum, the gate swinging open.
title: School Bell

describ: Wind moves through a bamboo grove beside the path — a dry, papery rustling with no pattern.
title: Bamboo in Wind

describ: At dusk the crickets start. By dark they're everywhere, under everything.
title: Evening Crickets

describ: Inside the departure hall: rolling luggage, announcements in three languages, someone running for a gate.
title: Airport Hall

describ: Pavement still wet — footsteps sound heavier, puddles catch reflections of neon.
title: Wet Pavement

describ: Rush hour intersection: the light changes and everything moves at once — engines, wheels, voices.
title: Rush Hour Crossroads

describ: Library interior: a kind of concentrated silence, disturbed only by page turns and climate control.
title: Library Quiet

describ: Neighborhood loudspeaker broadcasts community notices in a flat monotone — heard through closed windows.
title: Neighborhood Broadcast

describ: An old radio plays Cantonese pop from a repair shop doorway. The song fades as I pass.
title: Shop Window Radio

describ: Rooftop at dusk — wind shifts direction and the city's noise rises and falls like breathing.
title: Rooftop Wind

describ: The street sweeper comes through at midnight — bristles on asphalt, warning beeps, then silence again.
title: Midnight Sweeper

describ: Metro platform at peak hour: a wall of sound when the train arrives, then sudden vacuum as it leaves.
title: Metro Platform Rush

describ: Market closing time — vendors stack crates, unsold fish packed in ice, generators switched off one by one.
title: Market Closing

describ: A dog barking deep in an alley — persistent, answered by nothing. Then a door, then quiet.
title: Dog in Alley

describ: Inside an old building: water moving through pipes in the walls — a buried sound like digestion.
title: Pipes in Old Building

describ: Morning tai chi in the park — soft counting, breath, the occasional bird. No urgency.
title: Tai Chi in Park

describ: Garbage truck and morning street noise arriving together — the city starting its maintenance routine.
title: Morning Garbage Round

describ: A traditional opera rehearsal leaking through a community center wall — percussion first, then voice.
title: Opera Rehearsal

describ: Botanical garden waterfall — steady white noise that cuts off all city sound. A small acoustic island.
title: Botanical Garden Waterfall

describ: Underground passage: footsteps multiply and smear into continuous echo. Voices sound like they come from further away.
title: Underground Echo

describ: Sunday street market: dense, overlapping, cheerful — the loudest the city gets without being aggressive.
title: Sunday Market

describ: Afternoon thunderstorm — thunder rolling in from the west, rain arriving all at once, traffic stopping.
title: Afternoon Storm

describ: Evening riverside: the crowd is thick and the sound is too — food, laughter, a tour boat's engine.
title: Evening Riverside

describ: Fireworks heard but not seen — muffled booms from somewhere across the river, syncopated.
title: Distant Fireworks

describ: Last bus arriving — hydraulic hiss of the doors, the driver's radio playing quietly, passengers boarding in silence.
title: Night Bus Arriving

describ: From the balcony: the city as one continuous sound — no single source, just the hum of everything together.
title: Balcony Soundscape

describ: Restaurant kitchen at full speed — orders called, metal on metal, the extractor fan above everything.
title: Restaurant Kitchen

describ: Early morning along the canal — water lapping at stone steps, a barge engine idling in the mist.
title: Canal Morning Walk

describ: Inside the classical garden: wind through bamboo, a distant flute, footsteps on gravel that slow without reason.
title: Garden Silence

describ: Ping Jiang Road at midday — vendors calling prices, the clack of mahjong tiles from an open doorway, a delivery bike bell.
title: Old Street Market

describ: The evening bell at Cold Mountain Temple rolls across the water three times. The crowd falls quiet before it fades.
title: Temple Bell Evening

describ: Lakeside before the tourists arrive — breathing, soft footfall, the heron landing without a sound.
title: Tai Chi by the Water
